clinician.trajectory_summary: A 31-year-old male presented with a four-year history of an itchy, progressive rash on the face, trunk, and limbs, which started as macules and papules and eventually ulcerated. Physical examination revealed widespread hyperpigmented erosive plaques, nodules, and tumors covering over 95% of the body surface area. A skin biopsy confirmed Mycosis Fungoides with prominent spongiosis, and immunohistochemistry showed CD3 positivity. The diagnosis was further supported by an International Society for Cutaneous Lymphomas (ISCL) diagnostic algorithm score of 6 points, based on clinical and histological features. HIV serology was negative, and chest X-ray and abdominal ultrasound were normal, ruling out systemic involvement or other common conditions. No further clinical course or treatment information was available.
